title: USMNT’s Johnny Cardoso suffers ankle sprain ahead of World Cup roster reveal
content:
USMNT midfielder Johnny Cardoso has sustained a high ankle sprain in Atletico Madrid training, potentially putting his World Cup availability into question with Mauricio Pochettino due to name his squad on May 26 in New York City.

The 24-year-old suffered the injury this week after Atletico’s loss to Arsenal in the Champions League semi-finals, the club announced on Thursday, without putting a timetable on his return. “He will undergo physiotherapy and rehabilitation sessions in the gym, and the progress of his recovery will determine his return to competition,” the club wrote on X.

His appearance in the first leg vs. Arsenal made him only the fourth U.S. national team member to feature at that stage of Europe’s premier club competition — after DaMarcus Beasley, Tyler Adams and Christian Pulisic.

Cardoso has made 30 appearances in all competitions this season in his first campaign since signing from Real Betis, scoring once in the Champions League.

He has 23 caps for the USMNT but has only appeared once since last year’s Gold Cup, where he amassed 11 minutes on the pitch, in a March friendly against Belgium.

Following his planned 45 minutes against Rudi Garcia’s side, he returned to Atletico due to discomfort in his leg.

Analysis by senior soccer writer Henry Bushnell

Cardoso’s injury, in some ways, is a continuation of an unfortunate pattern: he has never been a reliable national team player.

Despite his obvious ability, even as he ascended from Internacional to Betis to Atleti, inconsistent performances and, yes, injuries have prevented him from establishing himself with the U.S.

The ankle sprain is yet another hinderance. After 45 solid minutes against Belgium in March, Cardoso was a strong contender to at least make the World Cup squad, perhaps as the top backup to Tyler Adams and Tanner Tessmann in midfield. And he still could be. But now, with the squad set to be named in less than three weeks on May 26, his inclusion is very much in question.

Without him, the depth of talent at that central midfield position would suffer. The other likely reserves are Cristian Roldan and Sebastian Berhalter — two MLS players with great character but obvious ceilings.

At the same time, though, Cardoso wouldn’t feel like a major loss because he has never really shown Pochettino and teammates what they would be missing.
